title: Chapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 5
content: Ah, am I an idiot?
To think I would try to deflect the Golden Ogre's arm with my sword.
I had pushed my Body Enhancement to its limits, but even so, my hand gripping the sword felt as if I had just struck a massive rock.
The Golden Ogre's arm, covered in tough skin and thick muscle, twisted grotesquely in an unnatural direction.
Just one more.
I had only managed to deflect its right arm so far.
No, but I should have bought a better sword, even if it meant stretching my budget.

If I could have severed both of the Golden Ogre's arms, I wouldn't be struggling this much. Even with Body Enhancement flowing into my sword, I couldn't swing it with full power, fearing it might break. I hated my own frugality.
The sword, propelled by the momentum of deflecting the right arm, collided with the left arm, shaking with the impact.
Then, an unexpected sensation coursed through both my hands.
The sword had embedded itself halfway into the Golden Ogre's left arm. My sword was nothing special, just a mass-produced item. I hadn't bothered with sharpness since I could enhance it.
So I knew, with my skill and the sword's dullness, I couldn't cut through the particularly tough part of the Golden Ogre's arm without worrying about it breaking.
So that's how it is, damn it.
I thought that if my hands weren't numb, I could have let go of the sword, but I steeled myself.
The Golden Ogre pulled back its left arm, causing my stance to falter.
From the moment I jumped in, my position had been reckless, leaving me unable to resist.
I could see the Golden Ogre's face twisting into a savage grimace.
I could feel its weight shifting onto its pivot foot.
Now, I wondered how far I would be thrown if it kicked me.
I watched the thick leg, like a log, swinging toward my abdomen and thought about such things.
Erika was truly astonished.
In response to Shin's incredible acceleration, she blurted out something as trivial as "fast."
And then she felt the weight of her own arrogance. Though she had said she would no longer underestimate Shin, the truth was she still did.
Continuing to witness Shin's swordplay, she felt that realization hit her.
The sword, wielded with unfamiliar footwork and body movements, could only be described as magnificent.
As Shin's sword aimed to sever the Golden Ogre's neck, Erika saw confidence in his movements.
No, that's not it.
The moment Erika realized this fact, an indescribable shock ran down her spine.
That person, Shin, was being careful not to break his sword.
What a waste, she thought, wanting to pick out a sword from her collection left at home that would suit Shin right away.
A master wouldn't choose their tools, but to unleash their full potential, they still needed the right tools.
Ah, what a waste.

Seeing Shin's swordsmanship, Erika became aware of feelings she had never experienced before. She wanted to be recognized, to be seen as amazing by Shin. She wanted to show him that she was not a hindrance beside him. Because of her past failure of turning a magic stone into ash, she couldn't help but think such things.

Thus, Erika poured her magic power into a single strike aimed at taking down the Golden Ogre. Her vast magic power, supported by a solid magic circle that an ordinary person couldn't construct. She believed that the fireball she unleashed would be enough to slay the Golden Ogre.
Because she thought that, Erika didn't let her guard down.
The roar of the Golden Ogre, which she thought she had defeated, hit her squarely due to her lack of experience. Erika instantly steeled herself.
Though countless insults toward herself floated in her mind, she swallowed them all and resolved herself.
So when Shin slipped between her and the Golden Ogre, she almost cried out in embarrassment.
Shin swung his sword in a reckless posture. Seeing him shout made her heart race. When was the last time she felt such reassurance from someone’s back?
It was a day filled with many points for reflection.
Erika drew her sword.
"I feel like I'm about to lose patience with my own foolishness."
As I struggled to avert my gaze from the approaching Golden Ogre's leg, I heard that voice. When using Body Enhancement, the timeline of thought and action often gets distorted.
And this time was no different.
The moment my enhanced hearing caught that voice, I found myself laughing before my thoughts could catch up.
The Golden Ogre's right leg, the one that was about to kick me, disappeared below the knee.
The Golden Ogre screamed in pain as it toppled over.
Blood gushed from the severed right leg, splattering across the field.
I barely managed to let go of the sword before getting caught up in the falling Golden Ogre and fell onto my rear.
"I really hate myself this time."
As Erika casually scattered the blood of the Golden Ogre that splattered toward her with wind magic, she muttered to herself.
"There are so many points for reflection that it's almost pathetic to count them."
Saying this, she sheathed her sword and took a step closer to the Golden Ogre.
The Golden Ogre struggled to distance itself from her with its intact left leg and functioning left arm.

"The power control was poor, my distance management was lacking, and my predictions for the next developments were naive. Not to mention the embarrassing thought of wanting to show off to Shin almost made me say something unbecoming of a lady."
The Golden Ogre desperately thrashed as it tried to get away from her.
Uneven furrows formed in the soft soil of the field.
"So what I'm about to do now is take out my frustrations. You might not understand, but I truly think I'm doing something terrible here, you know?"
The Golden Ogre crawled away, screaming.
"Whoa!"
I couldn't help but exclaim as I sat on the ground, watching the scene unfold.
I saw the shimmering golden magic power coalescing in the air with an absurd density.
A ridiculous number of fire arrows.
Erika let out a breath that resembled a sigh.

In an instant, the fire arrows rained down upon the Golden Ogre, and the sound of the arrows slicing through the air mixed with a multitude of explosions threatened to overwhelm my ears. I only caught a glimpse of the Golden Ogre for a moment.
I prayed for the Golden Ogre; what else could I do in such a scene?
As the swirling dust was blown away by wind magic, Erika turned back, looking inexplicably embarrassed. She wasn't proud or relieved from venting her frustrations.
She glanced at me shyly, her eyes downcast.
How cute is this? I stood up, brushing the dirt off my pants.
"I wonder if the magic stone is still there?"
I looked at the pockmarked field and said.
Fortunately, the crops had already been harvested, so there shouldn't be any complaints.
In an instant, Erika seemed to want to say something but swallowed her words, averting her gaze from me.
"Next time, it should be fine."
"Injuries?"
I asked, knowing full well there were none.
"That's my line, isn't it? I made a fool of myself."
Erika began to fidget with her hands in front of her chest. I thought I might never see her looking so hesitant again, so I etched that image into my mind.
"Um... thank you for saving me."
"You're welcome. And thank you as well; thanks to you, I didn't get kicked all the way to Faltarl."
Feeling embarrassed to express gratitude, how cute.
As I pondered this, Erika was still fidgeting with her hands in front of her chest.
What was that? I tilted my head in confusion.
"And... I'm sorry."
"What for?"
"Your sword got shattered into pieces."
I stroked the empty sheath, looked at the hole-riddled field, and then forced a smile. Even the second son of a poor viscount family could manage to put on a brave face.
To my surprise, the village chief hadn't fled.
When we returned to the village entrance after collecting the Golden Ogre's magic stone, we were met with the incredulous gazes of the village chief and the sister.
Not accustomed to such stares, I felt a bit suspicious, but Erika, perhaps more accustomed, spoke confidently.
"Village Chief, is this acceptable?"
Having explained on the way back to the village entrance, Erika now understood what the village chief had intended.
What the village chief had planned was simple: to save on the request fee to the Adventurer Guild.
When it comes to requests for subjugating strong monsters like the Golden Ogre, the fees paid to the guild are high.
Displeased with that, the village chief had hoped to lure adventurers with Bonbo as bait, expecting them to report the sighting of the Golden Ogre to the guild.
If dangerous monsters like the Golden Ogre are discovered near a village or town, they become urgent targets for subjugation.
In other words, they could get it done without having to pay a request fee.
Whether the village chief had knowledge of the Golden Ogre or not is unclear, but ogres are major urgent subjugation targets. He likely didn't care about the difference in color.
It's a method not typically used.
Of course, monsters don't consider human convenience, so they won't refrain from attacking based on human circumstances, and if such dangerous monsters attack, the village is bound to be devastated.
However, when certain conditions align, surprisingly many villages attempt this dangerous cost-saving method.
This village was perfect in terms of conditions.
It was close to a town with an Adventurer Guild, and while there was no barrier around the village, they had magic tools to ward off monsters.
Monsters tend not to approach places with unpleasant magic tools unless there's a reason. Fortunately, there were no casualties, and if they were attacked, they could escape easily with a carriage.
It was also close to a town with an Adventurer Guild, allowing for a quick response.
By accepting a little danger, they could save money.
The village chief likely thought he could save more than he originally anticipated by taking on more danger.
The village chief remained silent at Erika's words. He couldn't affirm adventurers.
His square face tightened as he pressed his lips together.
Erika probably didn't expect a reply either; she merely glanced at him before approaching the sister, who was leaning against the fence.
"Are you hurt?"
While receiving a disbelieving gaze from the sister, Erika calmly expressed concern for her injuries. The sister, surprised, responded.
"Better than before..."
At those words, Erika quickly checked the wound; the rib that had protruded was back beneath the skin. Though her breathing was still rough, she likely wouldn't die.
"I see, then we have a report of quest completion to deliver to the client."
Having confirmed the injuries, Erika hastily tried to leave, likely because she understood her position. It was not wise for us to get too close to church officials.
It was better for both parties to part quickly.
"Wait, wait! Who are you two?"
The sister called out to us as we tried to walk away.
I could have ignored her, and I intended to, but Erika stopped and said.
"We are adventurers, a married couple from Hekatai, known as the Longdaggers, Sister."
Erika lightly bowed her head, then walked away, ignoring the sister, who seemed to want to ask something else.
She muttered something about saying 'married couple' in a small voice, and I hoped it wasn't a complaint about the farce.
After reporting to the little girl that we had defeated the monster, we left the village.
Normally, we would have taken the magic stone fragments as an apology for the pockmarked field, but we left them there.
The village chief would likely handle that well.

While not as valuable as magic stones, magic stone fragments could still fetch a decent price. Since the Golden Ogre was a large monster, three of them would be enough to cover the compensation for the field.
Well, there wasn't much left from one of them.
"By the way, was it really okay for the village chief to stay like that?"
"About the request to the Adventurer Guild?"
"Yes, that's right."
Once the village was out of sight, Erika asked about the village chief's deception.
"There's no evidence, so it wouldn't matter if we told the Adventurer Guild."
"What about the testimony from that girl's father?"
"That was just because he was talking to us; if the guild asked, he'd deny it."
What the village chief did was betray the goodwill of the Adventurer Guild.
When the guild becomes aware of dangerous monsters, they voluntarily issue subjugation requests. That’s how the Adventurer Guild operates.
The guild's ideal of subjugating monsters for those without power is not just a hollow slogan.
"And if we start talking about it, it would never end."
Life in a farming village isn't easy. Many villages and settlements do similar things.
The guild understands this, so even if someone reports it, it would likely be brushed aside.
Many adventurers and guild staff come from farming villages.
"If you say so."
Erika concluded without much attachment to the matter.
Unexpectedly, we ended up spending a night in the village, and since the request had failed, it was a significant failure.
"Um... this is..."

At the Adventurer Guild counter, the guild staff, a woman, was staring blankly at the three Golden Ogre magic stones in front of her. By the way, she was the petite staff member who had handled our adventurer registration.
According to her name tag, her name was Lana.
"These are Golden Ogre magic stones."
Though it should have been a major failure, we had three Golden Ogre magic stones.
The amount the guild would buy them for would be sufficient compensation.
"This is an urgent subjugation target!"
The guild staff, Lana, exclaimed.
Magic stones obtained from monsters typically reveal their strength by appearance. To be officially recognized, they must be assessed using the guild's appraisal tools.
Though Lana should be accustomed to such things as a guild staff member, I wondered why she was so surprised.
"I'd like to request a buyout."
I conveyed my request.

The Adventurer Guild handles the buying of magic stones and materials obtained from monsters. The guild profits by selling these magic stones and materials to merchants, which is their main source of income.
"Why are you so calm about this?! Three of them!? Two Rank 1 adventurers took down three Golden Ogres!?"
For some reason, she seemed angry.
"W-wait a minute."
Lana twisted her body, looking as if she had seen something incredibly evil.
"Are you suggesting that we should make you Rank 7 as an exception for defeating three Golden Ogres?"
"I'm not saying that."
Is she still going on about this?
"More importantly, about the request we accepted..."
I glanced at the magic stones.
"I think it will probably be withdrawn."
At that, Lana made a face that said, 'I see.'
"That must have been quite a hassle."
She offered her sympathy but didn't delve deeper; she seemed to understand but didn't want to make it an issue.
"I have relatives in that village, so I want to personally thank you."
"In that case, please add some extra to the buyout price; my sword got ruined."
That's a separate issue, Lana brushed it off casually.
"However, if you're looking to buy a new sword, I can recommend a good shop."
That would be sufficient as compensation; after all, we were newcomers in this town.
If it was a recommendation from a guild staff member, it probably wouldn't be a bad shop.
"Then, let's proceed with the buyout."
"Understood."
While preparing the appraisal tools and documents, Lana spoke cautiously.
"You really won't say you want to be made Rank 7, right?"
I merely shrugged in response.
"Shin, what exactly is an adventurer's rank?"
This was during dinner at the dining hall.
Of course, Erika had never cooked before, and while I could manage, I couldn't make anything suitable for her.
The only dishes I knew were the kind adventurers made outdoors.
My master and fellow disciples never cared about taste when it came to food, so the dishes I learned were of that nature.
Thus, when those two tried to have their daily meals, it inevitably meant eating out.
Since it was generally difficult for adventurers to cook for themselves due to time constraints, Hekatai had numerous dining halls and taverns catering to adventurers, so we never had to worry.
"What do you mean by that?"
I asked, swallowing a fried potato.
By the way, we were dining at a slightly upscale restaurant thanks to the money from selling the Golden Ogre's magic stones.
"When you mentioned adventurer ranks a few times, I thought it represented strength. If that's the case, why hasn't your rank increased after defeating a Golden Ogre?"
That was a common misunderstanding.
"Indeed, an adventurer's rank is also a measure of strength."
After moistening my lips with water, I continued.
"But strength alone doesn't determine the rank. The completion rate of requests is also important for raising your rank."
I waved my fork like a baton as I explained.
Fortunately, Erika ignored my lack of decorum.
"Simply being strong isn't enough to achieve a high rank."
However──.
"Weak adventurers won't become high rank either."
I see, Erika said.
"If that's the case, our evaluation must be low since we failed the request."
Erika seemed to find that amusing and laughed.
"We're starting from scratch, or rather, from a negative."
Erika's eyes narrowed with delight, like a hunter spotting prey or a target.
"How interesting."
"I'm glad to see you having fun."
I said that from the bottom of my heart.
The next day, we set out to the district where the shops were gathered to do some shopping.
Our main goal was to procure Erika's equipment as an adventurer and to find a replacement for my shattered sword.
"This is..."
Erika presented me with an armor that was excessively revealing, her face a mix of confusion.
"Is this really okay?"
Indeed, I doubted the sanity of the shopkeeper who thought to display this.
"There are adventurers who prefer that kind of thing; the idea is that as long as you protect the vital areas, that's enough."
"I see."
Erika nodded, but I hoped she wouldn't choose that. I wasn't confident in my sanity. The shopkeeper, looking at me with hopeful eyes, seemed to have lost their mind, but I still had mine.
"By the way, wearing just that is only for the hardcore adventurers who prefer it."
The shopkeeper clicked his tongue, but when I glared at him, he awkwardly averted his gaze.
"Erika is a typical magic swordsman type, so while it's a valid option, I wouldn't recommend it..."
The shopkeeper kept making victory poses.
"Given the strength of your Body Enhancement, you could pass as a pure swordsman, so I wouldn't recommend it."
"That's true; even if you recommend it, it would be a bit troubling."
Saying that, Erika returned the overly revealing female armor to the shelf.
Behind Erika, the shopkeeper was gritting his teeth in frustration, but I ignored him.
What kind of shop is this? What kind of shopkeeper is that?
If it weren't for the recommendation from guild staff member Lana, I would have left immediately.
Yet, frustratingly, the selection was abundant, the prices were low, and the quality was good.
Aside from the shopkeeper's eccentricity, it was undoubtedly a good shop.
As I picked up a leather gauntlet made from monster hide, I pondered the absurdity of the world.
"By the way, Shin, do you have a preferred color?"
Erika asked while looking at the shop's items.
Color, a preferred color, huh?
"I don't have a particular one, but if I had to choose, it would be blue."
"Why is that? You seem to have nothing blue despite saying it's your favorite color."
I looked down at myself. To avoid showing dirt, I primarily wore black, and the only color was the brown of my leather belt. There was no blue to be found.
I answered with a wry smile.
"I like blue because it's the color of the sky. I don't wear it because I tend to feel self-conscious about things I like."
"I see, that's very much like you."
She seemed to agree wholeheartedly.
Which answer did she find convincing, I wondered?
Erika nodded thoughtfully.
"I've made my decision."
With that, Erika walked toward the counter.
Left behind, I thought I might as well wait outside, but I told her I would step out while she spoke to the shopkeeper at the counter.
I honestly confessed to myself that I thought the waiting time was longer than expected.
